    • isDynamicModeRequested

      public boolean isDynamicModeRequested()
      Whether the runtime configuration requests the element-specific difference-equation path through the generic simulation flag.

      This is a requested-mode indicator only. It does not prove that a subclass enters its stateful path; use getActivationStatus() for type-specific activation evidence where available.

      Returns:
      true when a SimulationInterface has calculateSteadyState == false

    • hasUnsupportedDynamicConfiguration

      public boolean hasUnsupportedDynamicConfiguration()
      Whether this element is configured in a way known to be incompatible with its audited capability.

      An algebraic element is a valid participant in a transient flowsheet while it remains in algebraic mode. It is a blocking configuration error only when its difference-equation mode is explicitly requested even though no audited dynamic implementation exists. A module is a composite container and is therefore not rejected merely because the container itself has no independent state; its nested contents are audited separately.

      Returns:
      true for an explicitly unsupported capability or algebraic non-module element forced into dynamic mode

    • hasIncompleteDynamicActivation

      public boolean hasIncompleteDynamicActivation()
      Whether a type-specific activation audit found a requested/enabled dynamic path with missing prerequisites.
      Returns:
      true when runtime activation configuration is incomplete

    • requiresCapabilityReview

      public boolean requiresCapabilityReview()
      Whether a custom transient implementation still needs engineering capability review.
      Returns:
      true for DynamicCapability.UNCLASSIFIED_DYNAMIC

    • hasInactiveAuditedDynamicState

      public boolean hasInactiveAuditedDynamicState()
      Whether an audited stored-state dynamic implementation is currently known to be inactive.

      Type-specific activation evidence takes precedence over the generic steady-state flag. For equipment families whose activation semantics are still unverified, the historical calculateSteadyState flag remains a conservative engineering review aid rather than a proof of actual runtime activation.

      Returns:
      true when the dynamic state is known or conservatively indicated to be inactive
